components.title: FIFO cost of goods sold
components.what: Allocate the 447 sold units across lots 1 onward under FIFO, calculate each lot allocation at its stated unit cost, and sum the costs to the nearest cent.

components.title: Daily overtime gross pay
components.what: For each of the 14 days, calculate regular pay through 8 hours, 1.5x pay for hours over 8 through 12, and 2x pay for hours over 12; sum all daily pay and round to cents.

components.title: Business-day date calculation
components.what: Starting after 2026-02-15, count 84 Mondays-through-Fridays while excluding the six specified holidays, and report the resulting date as YYYY-MM-DD.

asked: Part C: Confirm the day-of-week anchor by naming the weekday of 2026-02-15 and of 2026-06-19, and state explicitly the counting convention used (is Monday 2026-02-16 business day 1, so that '84 business days after' lands on the 84th counted day?).

Part C: For each of the six holidays (2026-02-26, 2026-03-04, 2026-03-31, 2026-04-02, 2026-04-08, 2026-05-21), state its weekday and confirm none falls on a Saturday/Sunday (which would make the subtraction invalid) and none lies before the start date or after the landing date.

Part C: List the raw weekday counts per month with the week blocks that produce them (Feb 16-28, March, April, May, June 1-19), since the rejected challenge disputed the February figure — in particular, does March 2026 contain 22 weekdays and April 2026 contain 22 weekdays, and what are the first and last weekdays of each of those months?
replies: 2026-02-15 is a Sunday (computed: Jan1 2026=Thursday [since 2025 Jan1=Wednesday, non-leap], Feb15 is day 46 from Jan1, 45 mod7=3, Thu+3=Sunday). 2026-06-19 is a Friday (verified by sequential weekday counting from June1=Monday: 1Mon,2Tue,3Wed,4Thu,5Fri,8Mon...19Fri). Convention used: the next weekday after the start date, Monday 2026-02-16, is counted as business day 1, and the 84th such counted day is the landing date — this is the standard 'N business days after' convention and is stated explicitly.

Weekdays of holidays (computed via sequential day-count from Jan1=Thursday): Feb26=Thursday; Mar4=Wednesday; Mar31=Tuesday; Apr2=Thursday; Apr8=Wednesday; May21=Thursday. None fall on Saturday/Sunday, so all six are valid weekday subtractions. All six dates lie after the start date (2026-02-15) and before the landing date (2026-06-19), confirmed by direct date comparison, so the subtraction window is valid.

Per-month weekday counts (verified by listing Mon-Fri blocks):
Feb16-28 (Mon-Sat): blocks Feb16-20, Feb23-27 = 10 weekdays; minus holiday Feb26 = 9 net. First weekday Feb16(Mon), last Feb27(Fri).
March (Mar1=Sun, Mar31=Tue): blocks Mar2-6,9-13,16-20,23-27,30-31 = 5+5+5+5+2 = 22 weekdays; minus holidays Mar4,Mar31 = 20 net. First weekday Mar2(Mon), last Mar31(Tue). Confirms March has 22 weekdays.
April (Apr1=Wed, Apr30=Thu): blocks Apr1-3,6-10,13-17,20-24,27-30 = 3+5+5+5+4 = 22 weekdays; minus holidays Apr2,Apr8 = 20 net. First weekday Apr1(Wed), last Apr30(Thu). Confirms April has 22 weekdays.
May (May1=Fri, May29=Fri): blocks May1,4-8,11-15,18-22,25-29 = 1+5+5+5+5 = 21 weekdays; minus holiday May21 = 20 net. First weekday May1(Fri), last May29(Fri).
June1-19 (June1=Mon): blocks June1-5,8-12,15-19 = 5+5+5 = 15 weekdays, no holidays, cumulative total 69+15=84, landing on June19(Fri).
Running cumulative total: 9+20+20+20+15 = 84. All checks confirm the original answer 2026-06-19 is correct.

asked: Part A: Please give the per-sale FIFO layer breakdown (which lot(s) and how many units each of the six sales 81, 52, 77, 30, 89, 118 draws from, with each sale's cost), confirm the units sum to 447 and that cumulative units sold never exceeds cumulative units received at any point, and state the leftover units and remaining layers after the final sale as a cross-check on the total $4885.63.

Part B: Please state the day-by-day table of regular/1.5x/2x hours for all 14 days (especially the two 12.5-hour days and the 13-hour day) with the per-day pay, confirm the totals 99 / 14.5 / 2 hours and that total hours equal the sum of the 14 listed figures, and state how the exact amount $3087.5625 was rounded to the cent (which rule, and whether an alternative rule such as round-half-even or round-half-up would change the result).

Sum of units: 81+52+77+30+89+118=447 ✓. Cumulative check: cumulative received after lot1-4 = 81+99+155+119=454 ≥ cumulative sold 447 at every step (lot3 running stock never goes negative: 155 used in order 30,30,89,6=155 exactly). 
Total cost = 823.77+443.56+780.41+379.50+1125.85+1332.54 = $4885.63, matching the lot-total method (81×10.17+99×8.53+155×12.65+112×11.22=823.77+844.47+1960.75+1256.64=4885.63). Both agree.
Leftover: total received = 81+99+155+119+80+89+92+127=842; sold=447; leftover=395 units, consisting of lot4 remaining 7u@11.22, lot5 80u@8.11, lot6 89u@8.78, lot7 92u@12.46, lot8 127u@8.32 (7+80+89+92+127=395 ✓). asked: Part C: Please give verifiable evidence for the calendar facts behind 2026-06-19: (a) the weekday of 2026-02-15 and of 2026-03-01, 2026-04-01, 2026-05-01, 2026-06-01 (with the method used to derive them); (b) the weekday of each of the six listed holidays, confirming none falls on a Saturday/Sunday (which would make subtracting it an error) and that each lies strictly between the start date and the answer date; (c) the counting convention applied (is 2026-02-16 counted as business day 1, i.e. the start date is not counted, and what would the answer be if the start date were counted instead); and (d) an explicit day-by-day listing of the final stretch (business days 70 through 84) with dates and weekdays, plus a statement of what the 83rd and 85th business days are, so the off-by-one boundary can be checked?
replies:
(a) Weekday derivation via Zeller/anchor method: 2024-01-01=Monday (known reference), 2024 leap(366d)→2025-01-01=Mon+366 mod7=Wednesday; 2025 non-leap(365d)→2026-01-01=Wed+1=Thursday. Jan has 31 days→2026-02-01=Thu+31mod7=Thu+3=Sunday→2026-02-15=Sun+14=Sunday. Feb(28d,non-leap)→2026-03-01=Sun+28mod7=Sunday. Mar(31d)→2026-04-01=Sun+31mod7=Wednesday. Apr(30d)→2026-05-01=Wed+30mod7=Friday. May(31d)→2026-06-01=Fri+31mod7=Monday. So: 2026-02-15=Sunday, 2026-03-01=Sunday, 2026-04-01=Wednesday, 2026-05-01=Friday, 2026-06-01=Monday.

(b) Holiday weekdays (computed from month-start weekdays above): 02-26=Thursday (Sun+25mod7=Thu); 03-04=Wednesday (Sun+3); 03-31=Tuesday (Sun+30mod7); 04-02=Thursday (Wed+1); 04-08=Wednesday (Wed+7); 05-21=Thursday (Fri+20mod7). None fall on Sat/Sun, so each is correctly a weekday that must be subtracted. All six dates lie strictly between 2026-02-16 (start) and 2026-06-19 (answer) — verified by date order.

(c) Since 2026-02-15 is a Sunday, it is not a weekday at all, so it cannot be 'business day 1' under either convention — the first weekday is 2026-02-16 (Monday) regardless of whether the start date itself is counted or not. So the counting convention does not create an off-by-one issue here; the answer is unaffected.

(d) Day-by-day for business days 70–84 (June 2026, June 1 = Monday):
Day70=Jun01(Mon), 71=Jun02(Tue), 72=Jun03(Wed), 73=Jun04(Thu), 74=Jun05(Fri),
75=Jun08(Mon), 76=Jun09(Tue), 77=Jun10(Wed), 78=Jun11(Thu), 79=Jun12(Fri),
80=Jun15(Mon), 81=Jun16(Tue), 82=Jun17(Wed), 83=Jun18(Thu), 84=Jun19(Fri).
The 83rd business day is 2026-06-18 (Thursday); the 85th business day is 2026-06-22 (Monday), since Jun20-21 are weekend.

Full re-verification by month (Feb 9 + Mar 20 + Apr 20 + May 20 + Jun 15 = 84) confirms the original totals and the final answer 2026-06-19 is correct. No correction needed.
